quizName: DMV Practice Test #12 16 Questions • Passing Score 12

questions.question: When you cannot avoid an object or uneven surface, what should you do?

options.text: Make sure the motorcycle leans to one side.
Speed up.
Swerve quickly.
Rise slightly off the seat so your legs can absorb the shock.

questions.correctAnswerText: Rise slightly off the seat so your legs can absorb the shock.
questions.explanation: If you must ride over an obstacle or uneven surface, approach it at a 90-degree angle. Slow down as much as possible. Keep your motorcycle upright. Rise slightly off your seat so your knees can absorb some of the impact. Just before contact, roll on the throttle slightly to lighten the front wheel.

questions.question: What does a shatter-resistant face shield do?

options.text: Protects a rider's face in a crash.
Protects only from dirt.
Offers less protection than goggles.
Should not be used with a helmet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protects a rider's face in a crash.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face during a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes, not your whole face. A face shield also protects you from dirt, dust, insects, rain, and pebbles.

questions.question: What should you do when turning on a motorcycle?

options.text: Keep your eyes focused near the front of the motorcycle.
Look through the turn toward where you want to go.
Turn your entire body to see through the turn.
Speed up before the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look through the turn toward where you want to go.
questions.explanation: When turning, look through the turn toward where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: Which action should you NOT do to stay safe when riding at night?

options.text: Increase your speed.
Reduce your speed.
Use your high beam headlight when possible.
Increase your following distance.

questions.explanation: To ride safely at night, reduce your speed. Use your high beam when not riding near other vehicles. Increase your following distance. Watch vehicles ahead of you. Their headlights show you the road. Their taillights bounce if they go over bumps.

questions.question: What is the danger of riding directly next to another vehicle?

options.text: You can be in the driver's blind spot.
It is safer than riding behind the vehicle.
It is safe because it limits your escape routes.
It should only be done during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can be in the driver's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Do not ride directly next to another vehicle. You may be in the vehicle's blind spot. If the driver cannot see you, they may change lanes without warning. Riding alongside a vehicle is also dangerous because it blocks your escape route if a hazard appears.

questions.question: What is the best sitting position when riding?

options.text: Your arms must hold you up.
You can easily reach the controls.
Your arms are straight when reaching the handgrips.
Your knees are away from the gas tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can easily reach the controls.
questions.explanation: Sit so you can use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up. Do not have to stretch to reach the handgrips. Your arms should be slightly bent when holding them. Keep your knees against the gas tank for balance.

questions.question: Which type of sign is rectangular in shape?

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.explanation: Signs about road rules, like speed limits, are usually rectangular. They are white with black letters or symbols. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, what should you do?

options.text: Keep riding because the wobble will fix itself.
Brake quickly.
Close the throttle to slow down.
Speed up quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Close the throttle to slow down.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up, as this makes the wobble worse. Grip the handlebars firmly. Slow down by gradually closing the throttle. Move your weight forward and down. Pull off the road as soon as you can. Then find and fix what is causing the wobble.

questions.question: What should you wear when riding a motorcycle?

options.text: Do not wear a jacket in warm weather.
Always wear a jacket, even in warm weather.
Wear shorts in warm weather.
Long shoelaces are not a concern.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always wear a jacket, even in warm weather.
questions.explanation: Always wear a long-sleeved jacket made of proper material when riding. This protects you even in warm weather and helps prevent dehydration. Always wear long pants. Tuck in your shoelaces so they do not catch on the motorcycle.

questions.question: How should you sit to control your motorcycle well?

options.text: Sit with your arms holding you up rather than steering.
Keep your knees against the gas tank for balance.
Let your feet hang off the footrests.
Sit far back so you must stretch to reach the handgrips.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the gas tank for balance.
questions.explanation: Keep your knees against the gas tank to maintain balance in turns. Sit so you can use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up. Sit forward enough so your arms are slightly bent when holding the handgrips. Keep your feet firmly on the footrests.

questions.question: How does a three-wheeled motorcycle handle curves?

options.text: The same as a two-wheeled motorcycle.
Differently than a two-wheeled motorcycle.
It should not be operated in curves.
It should use the shoulder when turning.

questions.explanation: A three-wheeled motorcycle or motorcycle with a sidecar turns differently than a regular two-wheeled motorcycle.

questions.question: When braking, what should you do?

options.text: Always use both brakes.
Use only the front brake.
Use only the rear brake on wet roads.
Use only the rear brake.

questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop, no matter what the road conditions are.

questions.question: What should you do before carrying a passenger in traffic for the first time?

options.text: Read books about carrying passengers.
Practice riding on an empty road.
Flash your lights so others can see you.
Practice riding on the road shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Practice riding on an empty road.
questions.explanation: Before carrying a passenger or heavy load in traffic, practice on a quiet road first. This helps you get used to how your motorcycle handles with the extra weight.

questions.question: The body removes about one alcoholic drink per hour. If someone drank eight drinks four hours ago, how many drinks are likely still in their body?

options.text: One drink
Two drinks
Three drinks
Four drinks

questions.explanation: Subtract the number of hours passed from the total drinks consumed. Eight drinks minus four hours equals four drinks remaining in the body.

questions.question: What does making eye contact with another driver mean?

options.text: It guarantees the other driver will yield to you.
It is not worth the effort.
It does not guarantee the other driver will yield to you.
It means the driver knows you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not guarantee the other driver will yield to you.
questions.explanation: Do not assume that eye contact with another driver means they will yield the right-of-way to you. Never count on it.

questions.question: Should your following distance at night be different from your following distance during the day?

options.text: Use a longer following distance at night.
Use a shorter following distance at night.
Keep the same following distance at all times.
Following distance does not matter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use a longer following distance at night.
questions.explanation: At night, it is harder to judge distances because you cannot see shadows or light contrasts. Always use a longer following distance when riding at night than during the day.
